page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.1-16 is an x86_64 compute shape within the flexible E4 series. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7J13 processor with a clock frequency of 2.55 GHz. Compute resources are provisioned with dedicated CPU allocation, supplying 1 physical core and 2 vCPUs using two threads per core. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of RAM, resulting in an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio that offers elevated memory density for an entry-level configuration.

Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs included on the instance. The server features no local storage, requiring operating systems and application data to rely entirely on network-attached block volumes. Network access includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The reliance on remote storage avoids physical disk management but introduces dependency on network-based input/output performance for read and write tasks.

Qualitatively, the shape provides cost efficiency for environments requiring meaningful memory capacity without paying for unneeded CPU cores. The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM balance targets workloads constrained by memory limits rather than compute throughput. Appropriate workload deployments include in-memory caching tiers such as Redis or Memcached, small transactional databases, background job runners, and lightweight container hosts.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.1-16 is a flexible virtual compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture. Driven by an AMD EPYC 7J13 processor operating at 2.55 GHz, the instance allocates 1 physical core configured with 2 threads to deliver 2 dedicated vCPUs. It features 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio that caters effectively to memory-intensive, low-thread operations. The configuration includes no local NVMe or SSD storage, requiring persistent storage needs to be handled via remote block volumes. Accelerated hardware is omitted, with zero GPUs present. Network connectivity is supported with one complimentary public IPv4 address. By delivering dedicated compute threads paired with an expanded RAM footprint relative to its core count, the instance serves as an efficient platform for lightweight databases, in-memory caching nodes, queue processing, and moderate web application serving.
